classification.difficultyReason: Find six alternative names for one marked angle across a figure with diagonal and side intersections.

content.prompt: Write six different names for the marked angle.

spec.description: ABCD with both diagonals meeting at the highlighted point E; horizontal FG passes through E. The marked angle at D lies between DA and DB.
spec.mathematics: F lies on AD, G lies on BC, and E lies on AC, DB and FG. The marked arms contain A and F, and B and E respectively. No right-angle, parallel or equal-length marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All source geometry, point names, highlighted E and selected arc are visible. Supplied angle names remain answer-only.

answer.short: Any six of $\angle ADB,\ \angle FDE,\ \angle ADE,\ \angle FDB,\ \angle BDA,\ \angle EDF,\ \angle EDA,\ \angle BDF$.
answer.worked: The vertex $D$ stays in the middle. One marked arm contains $A$ and $F$; the other contains $B$ and $E$. Reversing the outer letters gives eight possible names. Any six distinct names from $\angle ADB,\ \angle FDE,\ \angle ADE,\ \angle FDB,\ \angle BDA,\ \angle EDF,\ \angle EDA,\ \angle BDF$ are valid.
